description:
Find dialogue lines where a specific person or company is named in podcast transcripts.

## Three response modes

**`format="summary"` (default, wide scan).** Returns up to `limit` episodes (reverse-chronological), each with metadata + the first 10 mention-only lines (just the lines naming the entity, no surrounding dialogue). Use this to see *what's been said across episodes* and decide which episodes are worth reading in full. Paginate older episodes with `cursor`.

**`format="detail"` (narrow drill-in).** Requires `episode_slug`. Returns the full mention windows with `context_lines` of surrounding dialogue around each mention. Pass one slug for a single episode, or up to 10 comma-separated slugs (e.g. `episode_slug="all-in-200,all-in-201,all-in-202"`) to multi-get several episodes in one call. `limit`/`cursor` don't apply.

**`format="compact"` (screening).** The same episodes as summary, each with its mention count, the strings it was mentioned as, and the segments carrying the mentions (id, title, type, first mention time) — no dialogue lines at all, the smallest shape. `limit` and `cursor` page it exactly as summary. Use it to fan out over many entities or a long date range and decide where to read; the segment ids are citations, and `format="detail"` with the episode slug reads the lines.

## Workflow

Two patterns, depending on what you already know:

- **No specific episode in mind:** call `format="summary"` first to scan, then call `format="detail"` with the slug(s) of the episodes worth reading in full. For most questions (sentiment, recurring themes, who said what when), summary alone has enough signal and the second call isn't needed.

- **Already have the episode slug** (e.g. user mentioned the episode by name, or you have it from another tool like `particle_podcast_get_episode` or `particle_podcast_search_transcripts`): skip summary entirely and call `format="detail"` with `episode_slug` directly.

## Examples

*Wide scan, then drill in:* User asks "what has All-In said about OpenAI recently?". Call `format="summary"`, `company_slug="openai"`, `podcast_slug="all-in"`, `since="2025-11-01"`, `limit=20`. Read the mention lines per episode; if 2-3 episodes have substantive discussion, call `format="detail"`, `episode_slug="slug1,slug2,slug3"` for full context in one round-trip.

*Direct drill-in:* User says "In All-In #200 they discuss OpenAI's strategy — pull the full quotes". Call `format="detail"`, `episode_slug="all-in-200"`, `company_slug="openai"` directly — no summary needed.

## Who said it

The `guest_` filters keep only the mentions a matching guest spoke: `guest_field="banking-finance-and-investment"` with `guest_standing="established"` reads what established finance experts said about a company. When the question names who speaks ("doctors", "economists", "people in finance"), resolve the words with `particle_expertise_resolve` first and filter by the code; on `unresolved_reference`, resolve and retry rather than dropping the filter. A word no occupation names may name a capacity instead ("founders", "politicians"): pass it as `guest_capacity`. Each episode lists its identified speakers with their occupation codes, standing and seniority. For the split of all mentions across occupations or fields use `particle_podcast_get_share_of_voice`.

## When NOT to use this tool

For dialogue that *discusses* a topic without naming a specific person or company (paraphrase-tolerant search), use `particle_podcast_search_transcripts` instead — that one ranks segments by relevance to a free-text query.

For how often the subject comes up, or which shows mentioned it this week versus last, use `particle_podcast_get_mention_trends` instead of paging this tool once per period; its podcast slugs come back here as `podcast_slug` to read what a show said.

## Strongest first

With `speaker_statement_characteristics`, `sort="strength"` puts the episodes whose mentions carry the labels most clearly first: the most clearly negative takes on a company, the most confident predictions about a drug. This is the tool for the strongest lines about a subject; `particle_podcast_search_transcripts` refuses a subject without a topic and sends you here.

## Required inputs

One of `person_slug`, `company_slug`, or `entity_slug` is required: `person_slug` for a person, `company_slug` for a company, `entity_slug` for any other knowledge-graph entity (places, organizations, events, concepts). Resolve a name to a slug first with `particle_person_resolve`, `particle_company_resolve`, or `particle_entity_resolve`. Slugs are case-insensitive on input.

**How each line is said.** Lines in topic and interview segments end with their speaker statement characteristics, pole labels only, e.g. `_[positive · confident · future]_`: sentiment (negative/positive), certainty (hedged/confident), specificity (vague/specific) and temporal orientation (past/future). A pole label means the line clearly reads that way; `_[neutral]_` means it leans clearly on no axis; no brackets means the line was not read (short lines, intros, ad breaks). With `output_format=json` they are each line's `speaker_statement_characteristics` object, middle labels included.

**Filtering by how a line is said.** Pass `speaker_statement_characteristics` to keep only lines said a certain way: `{"sentiment": ["negative"]}` for criticism, `{"specificity": ["specific"], "temporal_orientation": ["future"]}` for concrete predictions, `{"certainty": ["confident"], "sentiment": ["positive"], "temporal_orientation": ["future"]}` for a high-conviction outlook. Put the topic, never the tone, in `semantic_search`. Every matched or mention line then carries labels the filter accepts.

**Without a topic.** On `particle_podcast_search_transcripts`, the filter alone with `episode_slug`, `speaker` or a `guest_` filter (no `semantic_search` or `keyword_search`) returns the strongest lines said that way, at most 50, strongest first: an episode's boldest predictions, or a person's most confident claims. Their `Match` row reads `characteristics`. For the strongest lines naming a person, company or entity, pass the filter with `sort: "strength"` on `particle_podcast_find_mentions` instead.

company_slug.description: Company slug, domain, or canonical ID (e.g. 'nvidia' or 'nvidia.com'). Resolves to the company's linked entity.

context_lines.description: Surrounding dialogue lines around each mention (1-20, default 2). Detail mode only — ignored in summary and compact.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous summary or compact response's cursor field. Summary and compact modes.

entity_slug.description: Knowledge-graph entity slug from particle_entity_resolve for the long tail that isn't a person or company — places, organizations, events, products, concepts (e.g. 'germany'). Use person_slug for people and company_slug for companies.

episode_slug.description: Episode slug(s) or canonical ID(s). For format='detail', required: pass one slug for a single drill-in or up to 10 comma-separated slugs (e.g. 'all-in-200,all-in-201,all-in-202') for a multi-episode drill-in in one call. For format='summary' or 'compact', optional filter to one episode.

format.description: Response shape. 'summary' (default) returns many episodes (reverse chron) with metadata plus the first few mention-only lines per episode — use this to scan and pick episodes to drill into. 'detail' requires episode_slug and returns one episode's full mention windows with surrounding dialogue context. 'compact' returns the same episodes as summary with the mention count and the segments carrying the mentions (id, title, type, first mention time) and no dialogue — the smallest shape, for screening many entities before reading any.

guest_capacity.description: Only mentions spoken by a guest who knows their field in this capacity (e.g. 'public_official' for politicians). particle_expertise_resolve names the capacity an everyday word means.

guest_field.description: Only mentions spoken by a guest listed under this ANZSRC 2020 field of research: a code, slug or title from particle_expertise_resolve.

guest_in_field.description: Only mentions spoken by a guest speaking within their own field (the guest the other guest_ filters select, when given).

guest_occupation.description: Only mentions spoken by a guest listed under this occupation: a SOC 2018 or ISCO-08 code, slug or title from particle_expertise_resolve, or a SOC group or everyday name (e.g. 'financial-and-investment-analysts' or 'physicians'). A word with no occupation filters by the field of research or capacity it names: 'investors' is field 350208, 'politicians' is capacity public_official.

guest_practicing.description: Only mentions spoken by a guest who still works in guest_occupation, which must be a SOC 2018 occupation or group.

guest_seniority.description: Only mentions spoken by a guest at this seniority or above.

guest_standing.description: Only mentions spoken by a guest whose standing is recognized this way: 'established' (conferred by others), 'self_described', or 'unverified'.

language.description: Restrict to episodes of podcasts in this language — ISO 639-1 code (e.g. 'fr'). Matches the podcast's primary language subtag, so 'fr' covers 'fr-FR'.

limit.description: Episodes per page (1-50, default 10). Summary and compact modes — detail returns one episode regardless.

output_format.description: Output serialization. 'markdown' (default) returns the LLM-facing rendering. 'json' returns the structured payload as JSON text — use only for programmatic chaining where exact field extraction matters; the JSON shape is larger and noisier for an LLM to read.

person_slug.description: Person slug or encoded person ID from particle_person_resolve, particle_entity_resolve, or the guest tools (e.g. 'sam-altman'). One of person_slug, company_slug, or entity_slug is required.

podcast_slug.description: Restrict mentions to a single podcast by slug, internal ID, or numeric iTunes ID. A particle.pro or Radar show link also works.

role.description: Constrain how the entity participates: guest, host, panelist, correspondent, or mention.

since.description: Only episodes published on or after this ISO 8601 date (e.g. 2025-01-01).

sort.description: Episode order. 'recency' (default) is newest first. 'strength' requires speaker_statement_characteristics and puts the episodes whose mentions carry those labels most clearly first (the most clearly negative takes, the most confident predictions), each episode's mentions strongest first. Pass the same sort with a cursor.

speaker_statement_characteristics.description: Keep only mentions said a certain way. This tool takes no topic text: the subject is person_slug, company_slug or entity_slug, and HOW it is spoken of goes here: criticism, skepticism or bearish takes → sentiment negative; praise, optimism or bullish takes → sentiment positive; predictions or forecasts → temporal_orientation future (add specificity specific for concrete predictions); high conviction → certainty confident; hedging → certainty hedged; concrete claims → specificity specific. Who speaks goes in the guest_ filters. Labels listed for one axis match any of them; axes combine with AND, so add only the axes the request names. Every mention line carries labels the filter accepts. Needs a subject with a knowledge graph entity: one matched only by name is refused. Example, criticism of the subject: {"sentiment": ["negative"]}. To narrow to a topic as well, call particle_podcast_search_transcripts with the subject's company_slug or entity_slug, the topic in semantic_search, and this filter.

certainty.description: How sure the speaker sounds. 'confident' for flat assertions and high conviction; 'hedged' for maybe, I think, it could, and other hedging; 'neutral' for neither.

sentiment.description: The statement's tone. 'positive' for optimistic, bullish, approving or praising lines; 'negative' for skeptical, bearish, critical or worried ones; 'neutral' for lines that clearly lean neither way.

specificity.description: Whether the line commits to something concrete. 'specific' for names, numbers, dates and mechanisms (concrete claims); 'vague' for generalities; 'neutral' for neither.

temporal_orientation.description: Where the line points in time. 'future' for predictions, forecasts, plans and expectations; 'past' for looking back; 'present' for how things are now.

until.description: Only episodes published on or before this ISO 8601 date.

name: particle_podcast_find_mentions
title: Particle Podcast Find Mentions
